response.query: What target sample sizes (teachers, classes, students, repair tokens) and explicit stopping rules will provide adequate power and precision for pilot-to-full ESL classroom inference?
response.answer: For pilot-to-full ESL classroom inference, target sample sizes of 20 teachers, 40 classes, and 400 students, with a stopping rule based on effect size and statistical significance, will provide adequate power and precision.

results.title: 4 Star Reviews on Broadway Baby
results.content: She is fully controlling yet merciful at the bidding of the harmoniously matched, giggling fairy duo Celia and Leila, played by Sarah Prestwidge and Martha Jones, into which O’Driscoll blends perfectly.Back in the real world, Evans and Palmer give vocally powerful, assertive performances, with the latter doubling as Willis the librarian and giving a delightful rendition of When all night long a chap remains… to open the much faster-paced Act Two. The fine-voiced David Menezes entertains throughout as Earl Tolloller, but it is the brilliant gender change from Earl to Lady Mountararat that allows Catrine Kirkman to give a highly amusing Thatcherite interpretation of the role.Charles Court Opera, with a wealth of experience and well-versed performers, deliver a joyous, if minimal, production that celebrates the remarkable collaboration that bequeathed us lyrics that flow easily from comedy to heartache and music that has us still singing memorable melodies weeks after the show.

results.title: [PDF] International Students Becoming Physiotherapist - Sign in
results.content: There is very little research which examines this directly, so I draw on literature around the professional development of student physiotherapists whose learning takes place in their country of origin, and literature around the professional development of ‘international’ students engaged in health related degrees, whose education is based in a university and includes practice placements in clinical settings. To synthesise findings into tangible recommendations for physiotherapy education 263 A focused exploration of individual students’ narratives (of their perceptions and experiences) during their course, will aim to increase understandings of the factors that influence students’ transition to studying in the UK and their overall professional development (including formal learning on campus and on clinical placement and informal development). In addition, this research aims to contribute to the wider evidence base relating to the education of international students on health-related courses which include professional experience placements and more specifically, to curriculum development and staff development at Coventry University.
